RQLBL-1.fp: 653400732-3351|req|- RQLBL-1: The later run exits without removing the label|+1333311384-1240
RQLBL-1.payload: MET: RQLBL-1 | WHY: When `race_lost: true`, `claim.sh` returns 1 without setting `_ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED`. `zbuild_claim_release` checks `_ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED` and returns early if empty; it never calls the release hook and never removes the label. DSRACE-4 asserts `_ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED` is empty and that `zbuild_claim_release` makes no hook call after a `race_lost` reply.
RQLBL-1.text: - RQLBL-1: The later run exits without removing the label

RQTIE-3.fp: 653400732-3351|req|- RQTIE-3: Either the claim writes its holder record itself, synchronously, before it re-reads, or the tie-break uses something that exists at claim time (for example when the label was added).|+1333311384-1240
RQTIE-3.payload: MET: RQTIE-3 | WHY: `claim_coordinator_claim` calls `_ccgl_race_note_post_v` synchronously before `_ccgl_read_labels` (the re-read). The `_CCGL_RACE_NOTE_AT == 0` guard fails closed if `created_at` cannot be determined from the POST reply. DSRACE-7 asserts POST_NOTE precedes ISSUE_VIEW in the call sequence, so removing the synchronous post or reordering it fails that assertion.
RQTIE-3.text: - RQTIE-3: Either the claim writes its holder record itself, synchronously, before it re-reads, or the tie-break uses something that exists at claim time (for example when the label was added).

RQTIE-2.fp: 653400732-3351|req|- RQTIE-2: If another run claimed it too, the run that claimed first wins|+1333311384-1240
RQTIE-2.payload: MET: RQTIE-2 | WHY: `_ccgl_race_note_first_v` sorts all trusted concurrent notes by `{t: created_at, id}` and returns `.holder` of the first. DSRACE-2 tests the loser scenario (earlier note belongs to `winner-run`) and the winner scenario (sole claimant). DSRACE-1 (And) tests that a winner note on page 2 is correctly identified.
RQTIE-2.text: - RQTIE-2: If another run claimed it too, the run that claimed first wins

RQTIE-1.fp: 653400732-3351|req|- RQTIE-1: When two runs claim an issue at the same moment, exactly one proceeds|+1333311384-1240
RQTIE-1.payload: MET: RQTIE-1 | WHY: `claim_coordinator_claim` posts a concurrent claim note, reads back all notes, finds the first by `created_at` then `id`, and returns `{"acquired": false, "race_lost": true}` for the loser; `zbuild_claim_acquire` in `claim.sh` refuses immediately on `race_lost: true` (rc 1). DSRACE-2 tests that the loser gets `race_lost:true`; DSRACE-5 tests that `race_lost:true` causes rc 1 without entering takeover. Reverting the arbitration block makes the loser return `acquired:true`, breaking the DSRACE-2 loser assertions; removing the `race_lost` check in `claim.sh` calls the takeover stub, breaking the DSRACE-5 `_takeover_calls` assertion.
RQTIE-1.text: - RQTIE-1: When two runs claim an issue at the same moment, exactly one proceeds

RQREB-1.fp: 653400732-3351|req|- RQREB-1: After adding the label, a run re-reads the issue|+1333311384-1240
RQREB-1.payload: MET: RQREB-1 | WHY: After posting the concurrent claim note, `claim_coordinator_claim` calls `_ccgl_read_labels "$issue"` before arbitration. DSRACE-7 asserts ISSUE_VIEW occurs after POST_NOTE and before GET_NOTES in the call sequence. Removing `_ccgl_read_labels` removes the ISSUE_VIEW call and all three DSRACE-7 ordering assertions fail.
RQREB-1.text: - RQREB-1: After adding the label, a run re-reads the issue

The answer holds.
ANSWER IAFND-2: wrong — DSRACE-7 tagged assertions in the current test verify POST_NOTE → ISSUE_VIEW → GET_NOTES order in a standalone call to `claim_coordinator_claim 8007`; removing `_ccgl_read_labels` removes the ISSUE_VIEW call and all three assertions fail. The answer holds.
ANSWER IAFND-3: wrong — DSRACE-2 loser assertions check `acquired: false` and `race_lost: true`; winner assertions check `acquired: true`. Both are present. The answer holds.
ANSWER IAFND-4: wrong — DSRACE-3 assertions check the PATCH file for id 99004 and its body content; all four sub-assertions are present. The answer holds.
ANSWER IAFND-5: wrong — DSRACE-4 assertions check `_ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED` is empty and that `zbuild_claim_release` makes no release call after `race_lost: true`. Both are present. The answer holds.
ANSWER IAFND-6: wrong — DSRACE-1 and DSRACE-7 ordering assertions enforce POST_NOTE before ISSUE_VIEW before GET_NOTES; both swapping and removing the synchronous write break them. The answer holds.

RQCMT-1.payload: MET: RQCMT-1 | WHY: When `winner != my_holder`, `_ccgl_race_note_update` PATCHes the note body to `"not started — concurrent claim: \`${winner}\` was first"`. RQADR-1.fp: 653400732-3351|req|- RQADR-1: Amend ADR-005: the first claim wins a tie, and how "first" is decided|+1333311384-1240
RQADR-1.payload: MET: RQADR-1 | WHY: ADR-005 §5 (amended 2026-11-27, #2534) documents: after adding the label, a note is posted as the holder record; the first note by `created_at` then `id` wins; the loser PATCHes its note to `"not started — concurrent claim: \`<winner>\` was first"`; `race_lost: true` skips the stale-takeover path. The `## Enforced by` section names the tests per statement.
RQADR-1.text: - RQADR-1: Amend ADR-005: the first claim wins a tie, and how "first" is decided
